title.zh: 卷13 志第8 音樂上
title.raw: 卷13 志第8 音樂上 Volume 13 Treatises 8: Music 1

translations.literal: Music, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Music 1

sentences.zh: 夫音，本乎太始而生於人心，隨物感動，播於形氣。

translations.literal: Sound originates in the Grand Beginning and arises from the human heart; as things are encountered it stirs the feelings, and spreads through form and breath.
translations.idiomatic: Sound has its root in the primordial beginning and is born in the human heart; stirred by what one encounters, it moves through body and breath.

sentences.zh: 形氣既著，協於律呂，宮商克諧，名之為樂。

translations.literal: Once form and breath are manifest, they harmonize with pitch pipes and tones; when gong and shang achieve harmony, this is called music.
translations.idiomatic: When physical expression takes shape, it aligns with the pitch standards; gong and shang harmonize, and this is called music.

translations.literal: Music (yue) means joy (le).
translations.idiomatic: Music is joy.

sentences.zh: 聖人因百姓樂己之德，正之以六律，文之以五聲，詠之以九歌，舞之以八佾。

translations.literal: The sage, because the people rejoice in his virtue, sets it right with the six pitch pipes, adorns it with the five tones, chants it in the nine songs, and dances it in the eight rows.
translations.idiomatic: Because the people delight in the sage's virtue, he regulates it with the six pitch pipes, ornaments it with the five tones, sings it in the nine songs, and dances it in the eight rows of performers.

sentences.zh: 實升平之冠帶，王化之源本。

translations.literal: Truly it is the crown and sash of an age of peace, the source and root of royal transformation.
translations.idiomatic: It is truly the crowning ornament of a flourishing age and the wellspring of civilizing rule.

translations.literal: The Record says: "Stirred by things, one moves, and so sound takes form.
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "Moved by things, the heart responds, and sound takes shape.

sentences.zh: 」夫人者，兩儀之播氣，而性情之所起也，恣其流湎，往而不歸，是以五帝作樂，三王制禮，標舉人倫，削平淫放。

translations.literal: " Man is the disseminated breath of the two principles, where nature and feeling arise; if one indulges its flow and sinks into it, going on without return, therefore the Five Emperors made music, the Three Kings established ritual, marked out human relations, and cut down excess and dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: Man is the breath of yin and yang made flesh, the seat of nature and emotion; left to run unchecked, feeling pours forth without return. That is why the Five Emperors created music and the Three Kings fashioned ritual—to set human relations in order and curb licentious excess.

sentences.zh: 其用之也，動天地，感鬼神，格祖考，諧邦國。

translations.literal: In its use it moves Heaven and Earth, touches spirits and ghosts, reaches ancestors, and harmonizes the states.
translations.idiomatic: Used rightly, it moves Heaven and Earth, stirs spirits and ghosts, draws near the ancestors, and brings the realm into harmony.

sentences.zh: 樹風成化，象德昭功，啟萬物之情，通天下之志。

translations.literal: It plants the winds and completes transformation, mirrors virtue and displays merit, opens the feelings of the myriad things, and communicates the will of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It plants moral influence and completes transformation, mirrors virtue and displays achievement, awakens the feelings of all living things, and gives voice to the will of the empire.

sentences.zh: 若夫升降有則，宮商垂範。

translations.literal: As for ascent and descent, there are rules; in gong and shang, models are handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent and descent follow fixed rules; gong and shang provide the standard for all modes.

sentences.zh: 禮逾其制則尊卑乖，樂失其序則親疏亂。

translations.literal: If ritual exceeds its measure, high and low are at odds; if music loses its order, near and far fall into confusion.
translations.idiomatic: When ritual oversteps its proper form, rank and station are thrown into disorder; when music loses its sequence, intimacy and distance are confused.

sentences.zh: 禮定其象，樂平其心，外敬內和，合情飾貌，猶陰陽以成化，若日月以為明也。

translations.literal: Ritual fixes the outward image; music settles the inner heart—outward reverence, inward harmony, joining feeling and adorning appearance, like yin and yang completing transformation, like sun and moon giving light.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual defines the outward form; music calms the inner heart. Outward reverence and inward harmony join feeling to appearance, as yin and yang complete transformation and sun and moon give light.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「大夫無故不撤懸，士無故不撤琴瑟。

translations.literal: The Record says: "A grandee, without special cause, does not remove his suspended bells; a gentleman, without special cause, does not put away his zithers.
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "A grandee does not remove his suspended bells without good cause; a gentleman does not put away his zither and lute without good cause.

sentences.zh: 」聖人造樂，導迎和氣，惡情摒退，善心興起。

translations.literal: " The sage creates music to guide and welcome harmonious qi, to drive off evil feeling and raise up good intent.
translations.idiomatic: The sage creates music to welcome harmonious qi, drive away corrupt emotion, and awaken virtuous intent.

sentences.zh: 伊耆有葦籥之音，伏犧有網罟之詠，葛天八闋，神農五弦，事與功偕，其來已尚。

translations.literal: Emperor Yi had the sound of reed pipes; Fuxi had the song of nets and snares; Getian had eight airs; Shennong had five strings—the deed and the achievement go together; the antiquity of it is already high.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yi had reed-pipe music; Fuxi had the song of the hunting net; Getian had eight songs; Shennong had the five-string lute—each deed matched its music, and the tradition reaches far back.

sentences.zh: 黃帝樂曰《咸池》，帝嚳曰《六英》，帝顓頊曰《五莖》，帝堯曰《大章》，帝舜曰《簫韶》，禹曰《大夏》，殷湯曰《護》，武王曰《武》，周公曰《勺》。

translations.literal: Yellow Emperor's music was called "Xian Pool"; Emperor Ku's was "Six Splendors"; Emperor Zhuanxu's was "Five Stalks"; Emperor Yao's was "Great Pattern"; Emperor Shun's was "Xiao Shao"; Yu's was "Great Xia"; Tang of Yin's was "Hu"; King Wu's was "Wu"; the Duke of Zhou's was "Shao."
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor's music was called Xian Pool; Emperor Ku's, Six Splendors; Emperor Zhuanxu's, Five Stalks; Emperor Yao's, Great Pattern; Emperor Shun's, Xiao Shao; Yu's, Great Xia; Tang of Yin's, Hu; King Wu's, Wu; and the Duke of Zhou's, Shao.

sentences.zh: 教之以風賦，弘之以孝友，大禮與天地同節，大樂與天地同和，禮意風猷，樂情膏潤。

translations.literal: They taught by wind and fu, enlarged by filial piety and brotherhood; great ritual shares its measure with Heaven and Earth, great music shares its harmony with Heaven and Earth—ritual's meaning is the wind's current, music's feeling is the moistening balm.
translations.idiomatic: They taught through the Odes and rhapsodies, spreading filial piety and brotherly duty; great ritual keeps pace with Heaven and Earth, great music harmonizes with Heaven and Earth—ritual carries moral purpose, music nourishes the heart.

translations.literal: The Tradition says: "If there is to be a true king, benevolence comes only after several generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition says: "When a true king appears, benevolent rule takes generations to ripen.

sentences.zh: 」成、康化致升平，刑厝而不用也。

translations.literal: " The transformations of Cheng and Kang reached ascendant peace, and punishments were laid aside unused.
translations.idiomatic: The reigns of Kings Cheng and Kang brought an age of peace so complete that punishments fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 古者天子聽政，公卿獻詩。

translations.literal: In antiquity when the Son of Heaven heard affairs of state, the ministers and grandees presented odes.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Son of Heaven listened to governance while ministers and grandees presented poems.

translations.literal: The people of Qin had their own compositions; this Way was rarely heard.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin had their own music, but this tradition was rarely heard thereafter.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖時，叔孫通爰定篇章，用祀宗廟。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Gaozu of Han, Shusun Tong thereupon fixed the ritual sections for use in sacrifices to the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han Gaozu, Shusun Tong fixed the ritual sections for ancestral temple sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 唐山夫人能楚聲，又造房中之樂。

translations.literal: Lady Tangshan could perform Chu songs, and also created music for the inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Tangshan, skilled in Chu songs, also composed chamber music.

sentences.zh: 武帝裁音律之響，定郊丘之祭，頗雜謳謠，非全雅什。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu trimmed the resonance of pitch and tone, fixed the sacrifices at the suburban altars, and mixed in many popular ballads—not wholly orthodox odes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu refined pitch and tone, established suburban sacrifices, and incorporated many folk songs—not entirely orthodox court odes.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝時，樂有四品：一曰《大予樂》，郊廟上陵之所用焉。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming of Han, music had four grades: first, Great Imperial Music, used at suburban rites, ancestral temples, and imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han Mingdi, music fell into four categories: first, Great Imperial Music, used at suburban sacrifices, ancestral temples, and imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 則《易》所謂「先王作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考」者也。

translations.literal: This is what the Changes calls "the former kings made music to honor virtue, and in the Yin season offered to the Lord on High, matching the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: This is what the Book of Changes means by "the former kings made music to honor virtue, and in the Yin season offered to the Lord on High, pairing him with the ancestors."

sentences.zh: 二曰雅頌樂，辟雍饗射之所用焉。

translations.literal: Second, Ya and Song music, used at the Bright Hall feasts and archery rites.
translations.idiomatic: Second, Ya and Song music, used at Bright Hall banquets and archery ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 則《孝經》所謂「移風易俗，莫善於樂」者也。

translations.literal: This is what the Classic of Filial Piety calls "to shift the winds and change custom, nothing is better than music."
translations.idiomatic: This is what the Classic of Filial Piety means by "nothing transforms custom better than music."

sentences.zh: 三曰黃門鼓吹樂，天子宴群臣之所用焉。

translations.literal: Third, Yellow Gate Impromptu Music, used when the Son of Heaven feasted his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Third, Yellow Gate Impromptu Music, performed when the Son of Heaven feasted his ministers.

sentences.zh: 則《詩》所謂「坎坎鼓我，蹲蹲儛我」者也。

translations.literal: This is what the Odes call "beat the drums for us, dance for us in ranks."
translations.idiomatic: This is what the Odes mean by "beat the drums for us, dance for us in ranks."

sentences.zh: 其四曰短簫鐃歌樂，軍中之所用焉。

translations.literal: The fourth is Short Flute and Naoge Music, used in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, Short Flute and Naoge Music, used in military campaigns.

sentences.zh: 黃帝時，岐伯所造，以建武揚德，風敵勵兵，則《周官》所謂「王師大捷，則令凱歌」者也。

translations.literal: In the time of the Yellow Emperor, Qibo created it to establish martial glory, display virtue, stir the enemy, and encourage the troops—what the Offices of Zhou calls "when the royal army wins a great victory, victory songs are ordered."
translations.idiomatic: Created by Qibo in the Yellow Emperor's time, it proclaimed martial glory, displayed virtue, intimidated the enemy, and roused the troops—what the Rites of Zhou calls "when the royal army wins a great victory, victory songs are commanded."

sentences.zh: 又采百官詩頌，以為登歌，十月吉辰，始用烝祭。

translations.literal: They also gathered odes and hymns from the hundred offices to serve as ascent songs; on the auspicious day of the tenth month, the steam sacrifice was first performed.
translations.idiomatic: They also collected odes and hymns from officials of every rank for ascent songs, and on the auspicious tenth month performed the steam sacrifice.

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Dong Zhuo, orthodox music was wholly scattered.
translations.idiomatic: During Dong Zhuo's rebellion, orthodox music was completely lost.

sentences.zh: 漢雅樂郎杜夔，能曉樂事，八音七始，靡不兼該。

translations.literal: Du Kui, director of Han's elegant music, understood musical affairs; of the eight sounds and seven beginnings, none escaped his mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Kui of Han's elegant music bureau understood every aspect of music—the eight sounds and seven pitch origins were all within his grasp.

sentences.zh: 魏武平荊州，得夔，使其刊定雅律。

translations.literal: When Cao Wu pacified Jing Province he obtained Kui and had him edit and fix the elegant pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao pacified Jing Province he obtained Du Kui and had him revise the orthodox pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 魏有先代古樂，自夔始也。

translations.literal: Wei had ancient music of former ages—beginning with Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ancient music of former dynasties began with Du Kui.

sentences.zh: 自此迄晉，用相因循，永嘉之寇，盡淪胡羯。

translations.literal: From this down to Jin they followed one another; in the Yongjia invasion everything was lost to the Hu and Jie.
translations.idiomatic: From then until Jin the tradition was handed down, but the Yongjia invasion swept it all away among the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 於是樂人南奔，穆皇羅鐘磬，苻堅北敗，孝武獲登歌。

translations.literal: Thereupon musicians fled south; Emperor Mu gathered bells and chime-stones; when Fu Jian was defeated in the north, Emperor Xiaowu recovered the ascent songs.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians fled south; Emperor Mu of Jin gathered bells and stones; when Fu Jian was defeated in the north, Emperor Xiaowu recovered the ascent songs.

sentences.zh: 晉氏不綱，魏圖將霸，道武克中山，太武平統萬，或得其宮懸，或收其古樂，于時經營是迫，雅器斯寢。

translations.literal: Jin lost its discipline; Wei was about to rise to hegemony—Daowu took Zhongshan, Taiwu pacified Tongwan; sometimes they obtained court bell-sets, sometimes they collected ancient music; at the time urgent affairs pressed, and elegant instruments were set aside.
translations.idiomatic: As Jin fell into disorder and Wei rose toward dominance, Daowu conquered Zhongshan and Taiwu pacified Tongwan—sometimes capturing court bell-sets, sometimes gathering ancient music—but urgent statecraft left elegant instruments neglected.

sentences.zh: 孝文頗為詩歌，以勖在位，謠俗流傳，布諸音律。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen of Wei often composed songs and poems to encourage those in office; ballads spread among the people and were arranged to pitch and mode.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen of Wei composed songs and poems to encourage his officials; popular ballads spread and were set to pitch and mode.

sentences.zh: 大臣馳騁漢、魏，旁羅宋、齊，功成奮豫，代有製作。

translations.literal: Great ministers ranged through Han and Wei, gathered from Song and Qi; after success they rejoiced, and each age had its own compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers drew on Han and Wei traditions and collected from Song and Qi; after each triumph they composed celebratory music, and every age produced its own works.

sentences.zh: 莫不各揚廟舞，自造郊歌，宣暢功德，輝光當世，而移風易俗，浸以陵夷。

translations.literal: None failed to display their own temple dances and create their own suburban hymns, proclaiming merit and virtue, shining glory on the age—yet in shifting the winds and changing custom, decline set in by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Each dynasty staged its own temple dances and composed its own suburban hymns, proclaiming merit and virtue in the light of the age—yet in transforming custom, decline crept in by degrees.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝本自諸生，博通前載，未及下車，意先風雅，爰詔凡百，各陳所聞。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang was originally a scholar, broadly versed in earlier records; before he even left his carriage, his mind was already set on elegance and refinement, and he thereupon ordered all to state what they knew.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang began as a scholar steeped in earlier learning; even before taking the throne his heart was set on restoring refined music, and he ordered everyone to submit their views.

sentences.zh: 帝又自糾擿前違，裁成一代。

translations.literal: The Emperor also himself corrected past errors and shaped a standard for the age.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor himself corrected past errors and established standards for his age.

sentences.zh: 周太祖發跡關隴，躬安戎狄，群臣請功成之樂，式遵周舊，依三材而命管，承六典而揮文。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor of Zhou rose in Guanlong, personally settled the frontier tribes; his ministers requested music of achieved merit, following Zhou antiquity, ordering pipes according to the three materials and wielding text according to the six canons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's Grand Ancestor rose in Guanlong and personally pacified the frontier tribes; his ministers requested victory music following Zhou antiquity, ordering pipes by the three materials and composing texts by the six classics.

sentences.zh: 而《下武》之聲，豈姬人之唱，登歌之奏，協鮮卑之音，情動於中，亦人心不能已也。

translations.literal: Yet the sound of "Xia Wu"—could that be the song of the Ji people? The ascent songs harmonized with Xianbei tones; feeling stirred within—this too is what the human heart cannot restrain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the melody of Xia Wu—was that truly a Ji song? The ascent songs harmonized with Xianbei tones; feeling stirred within—the human heart cannot always be restrained.

sentences.zh: 昔仲尼返魯，風雅斯正，所謂有其藝而無其時。

translations.literal: Formerly when Confucius returned to Lu, the Airs and Elegances were set right—what is called having the art but not the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Confucius returned to Lu, the Airs and Elegances were set right—yet he had the art without the opportune moment.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命惟新，八州同貫，制氏全出於胡人，迎神猶帶于邊曲。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the mandate anew, the eight provinces were united; the music masters all came from barbarian peoples, and the hymns welcoming the spirits still carried frontier melodies.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Sui received the mandate, the eight provinces were united—but the music masters were mostly of barbarian origin, and hymns welcoming the spirits still bore frontier melodies.

sentences.zh: 及顏、何驟請，頗涉雅音，而繼想聞《韶》，去之彌遠。

translations.literal: When Yan and He urgently petitioned, they touched somewhat on elegant tones, yet in continuing to long for Shao music, they moved ever farther from it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan and He urgently petitioned, they touched on orthodox tones—but those who yearned for Shao music were ever farther from attaining it.

sentences.zh: 若夫二南斯理，八風揚節，順序旁通，妖淫屏棄，宮徵流唱，翱翔率舞，弘仁義之道，安性命之真，君子益厚，小人無悔，非大樂之懿，其孰能與於此者哉！

translations.literal: As for the principle of the Two Souths, the eight winds raising their measure, sequence passing through on every side, licentious and corrupt music cast aside, palace and pitch modes flowing in song, soaring and leading the dance—expanding the Way of humaneness and righteousness, settling the truth of life and nature, gentlemen growing deeper, common men without regret—if not the excellence of great music, who could share in this!
translations.idiomatic: When the Two Souths govern rightly, the eight winds raise their proper measure, order passes freely in every direction, licentious music is cast aside, palace modes flow in song, dancers rise and wheel in flight—expanding humaneness and righteousness, securing the truth of life, deepening the gentleman and leaving no regret among common men—if this is not the glory of great music, what is?

sentences.zh: 是以舜詠《南風》而虞帝昌，紂歌北鄙而殷王滅。

translations.literal: Therefore when Shun sang the "Southern Winds," Emperor Yu flourished; when Zhou sang the northern frontier, King Yin perished.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun sang the Southern Winds, the Yu dynasty flourished; when Zhou sang frontier melodies of the north, the Yin dynasty fell.

translations.literal: When great music is not disordered, royal governance stands within it.
translations.idiomatic: When great music keeps its order, royal governance rests secure.

sentences.zh: 故錄其不相因襲，以備於志。

translations.literal: Therefore I record what does not simply follow in succession, to preserve it in this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore record what does not merely repeat inherited forms, preserving it in this treatise.

sentences.zh: 《周官》大司樂一千三百三十九人。

translations.literal: In the Offices of Zhou, the Grand Music Master had 1,339 persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Music Master of the Offices of Zhou numbered 1,339 persons.

sentences.zh: 漢郊廟及武樂，三百八十人。

translations.literal: Han's suburban temples and martial music: 380 persons.
translations.idiomatic: Han's suburban temples and martial music employed 380 persons.

sentences.zh: 煬帝矜奢，頗玩淫曲，御史大夫裴蘊，揣知帝情，奏括周、齊、梁、陳樂工子弟，及人間善聲調者，凡三百餘人，並付太樂。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang indulged extravagance and dabbled much in licentious tunes; Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, gauging the Emperor's taste, memorialized to gather musicians' sons and daughters from Zhou, Qi, Liang, and Chen, and all skilled in fine tones among the people—more than 300 in all—and assign them to the Grand Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang indulged extravagance and favored licentious tunes; Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, reading the Emperor's taste, memorialized to gather musicians' children from Zhou, Qi, Liang, and Chen and all skilled performers among the people—more than 300 in all—and assign them to the Grand Music Office.

translations.literal: Actors and singers intermixed—all came and gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Actors and singers mingled together, and all converged there.

sentences.zh: 其哀管新聲，淫弦巧奏，皆出鄴城之下，高齊之舊曲雲。

translations.literal: The mournful pipes' new sounds and the licentious strings' clever playing all came from below Ye city—the old tunes of Northern Qi, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The new sounds of mournful pipes and the clever playing of licentious strings all came from below Ye city—the old tunes of Northern Qi, it is said.

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Liang house, music followed Qi's old tradition.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Liang, music followed the old Qi tradition.

sentences.zh: 武帝思弘古樂，天監元年，遂下詔訪百僚曰：「夫聲音之道，與政通矣，所以移風易俗，明貴辨賤。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to expand ancient music; in the first year of Tianjian he issued an edict asking the hundred officials: "The Way of sound and music connects with governance; therefore it shifts the winds and changes custom, clarifying noble and base.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sought to restore ancient music; in Tianjian year 1 he issued an edict asking the officials: "The Way of music connects with governance—it shifts custom, clarifies rank, and distinguishes noble from base.

sentences.zh: 而《韶》、《護》之稱空傳，《鹹》、《英》之實靡托，魏晉以來，陵替滋甚。

translations.literal: Yet the names of Shao and Hu are transmitted empty; the reality of Xian and Ying has no resting place; from Wei and Jin onward, decline grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the names of Shao and Hu survive only as empty titles; the substance of Xian and Ying has no firm foundation; from Wei and Jin onward decline grew ever worse.

sentences.zh: 遂使雅鄭混淆，鐘石斯謬，天人缺九變之節，朝宴失四懸之儀。

translations.literal: Thus elegant and popular music were confused, bells and stones went astray; Heaven and man lacked the nine transformations, court feasts lost the four suspended sets.
translations.idiomatic: Elegant and popular music were confused, bells and stones misaligned; Heaven and man lacked the nine ritual transformations, and court banquets lost the four suspended bell-sets.

sentences.zh: 朕昧旦坐朝，思求厥旨，而舊事匪存，未獲厘正，寤寐有懷，所為歎息。

translations.literal: I rise at dawn to hold court, thinking to seek the root of this, yet old affairs are not preserved and I have not been able to set it right; waking and sleeping I have this concern, and sigh for it.
translations.idiomatic: I rise at dawn to hold court, seeking the root of this problem, yet old records are lost and I cannot set matters right—this weighs on me waking and sleeping.

sentences.zh: 卿等學術通明，可陳其所見。

translations.literal: You, with your learning clear and penetrating, may state what you see.
translations.idiomatic: You whose learning is clear and penetrating—state what you know.

sentences.zh: 」於是散騎常侍、尚書僕射沈約奏答曰：「竊以秦代滅學，《樂經》殘亡。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Attendant Cavalier and Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Shen Yue memorialized in reply: "I venture to think that in the Qin age learning was extinguished and the Music Classic was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Cavalier and Vice Minister Shen Yue replied: "In the Qin, learning was destroyed and the Music Classic lost.

sentences.zh: 至於漢武帝時，河間獻王與毛生等，共采《周官》及諸子言樂事者，以作《樂記》。

translations.literal: Down to the time of Emperor Wu of Han, the King of Hejian and Mao Sheng and others together gathered passages on music from the Offices of Zhou and various masters to compose the Record of Music.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Wu of Han's time, the King of Hejian and Mao Sheng gathered passages on music from the Offices of Zhou and various masters to compose the Record of Music.

sentences.zh: 其內史丞王定，傳授常山王禹。

translations.literal: Wang Ding, assistant director of the palace, transmitted it to Changshan Wang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ding, assistant director of the palace, transmitted it to Changshan Wang Yu.

sentences.zh: 劉向校書，得《樂記》二十三篇，與禹不同。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang collated books and obtained twenty-three chapters of the Record of Music, differing from Yu's version.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang collated books and found twenty-three chapters of the Record of Music, differing from Yu's version.

sentences.zh: 向《別錄》，有《樂歌詩》四篇、《趙氏雅琴》七篇、《師氏雅琴》八篇、《龍氏雅琴》百六篇。

translations.literal: In Xiang's Separate Record there were four chapters of Music Odes and Songs, seven chapters of Master Zhao's Elegant Zither, eight chapters of Master Shi's Elegant Zither, and 106 chapters of Master Long's Elegant Zither.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiang's Separate Record were four chapters of Music Odes and Songs, seven of Master Zhao's Elegant Zither, eight of Master Shi's Elegant Zither, and 106 of Master Long's Elegant Zither.

translations.literal: Only these.
translations.idiomatic: Only these survived.

sentences.zh: 《晉中經簿》無複樂書，《別錄》所載，已覆亡逸。

translations.literal: The Jin Central Canon Catalogue has no music books further; what the Separate Record listed has already perished and been lost.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Central Canon Catalogue lists no further music books; what the Separate Record recorded is already lost.

sentences.zh: 案漢初典章滅絕，諸儒捃拾溝渠牆壁之間，得片簡遺文，與禮事相關者，即編次以為禮，皆非聖人之言。

translations.literal: Considering that at the beginning of Han the canonical statutes were extinguished, the various Ru gathered stray texts from ditches and walls; any fragmentary surviving passage related to ritual affairs was arranged as ritual—all not the words of sages.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Han the canonical statutes were lost; scholars gathered stray fragments from ditches and walls—any scrap related to ritual was arranged as ritual, though none were the words of sages.

sentences.zh: 《月令》取《呂氏春秋》，《中庸》、《表記》、《防記》、《緇衣》皆取《子思子》，《樂記》取《公孫尼子》，《檀弓》殘雜，又非方幅典誥之書也。

translations.literal: Monthly Ordinance was taken from Master Lü's Spring and Autumn; Doctrine of the Mean, Record of Conduct, Record of Mourning, and Black Robe were taken from Master Zisi; Record of Music was taken from Gongsun Ni; Record of the Bow is a jumbled remnant—not a canonical book of proper scope.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly Ordinance came from Master Lü's Spring and Autumn; Doctrine of the Mean, Record of Conduct, Record of Mourning, and Black Robe from Master Zisi; Record of Music from Gongsun Ni; Record of the Bow is a jumbled remnant—not a canonical text of proper scope.

sentences.zh: 禮既是行己經邦之切，故前儒不得不補綴以備事用。

translations.literal: Ritual is urgent for personal conduct and governing the state, so former scholars had no choice but to patch and join to supply what practice required.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is urgent for personal conduct and statecraft, so earlier scholars had no choice but to patch and supplement what practice required.

sentences.zh: 樂書事大而用緩，自非逢欽明之主，製作之君，不見詳議。

translations.literal: Music books treat great affairs but are slow in use; unless one meets a reverent and enlightened lord, a founding ruler, one does not see them discussed in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Music treats great affairs but is slow to put into practice; unless one meets a reverent and enlightened sovereign, it is rarely discussed in detail.

sentences.zh: 漢氏以來，主非欽明，樂既非人臣急事，故言者寡。

translations.literal: Since the Han house, lords were not reverent and enlightened, and music was not an urgent matter for ministers—therefore few spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han, rulers were seldom reverent and enlightened, and music was no urgent concern for ministers—so few spoke of it.

sentences.zh: 陛下以至聖之德，應樂推之符，實宜作樂崇德，殷薦上帝。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with utmost sage virtue, corresponds to the token of music's elevation—you should truly make music to honor virtue and in the Yin season offer to the Lord on High.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, with utmost sage virtue, bears the token of music's elevation—you should make music to honor virtue and in the Yin season offer to the Lord on High.

translations.literal: Yet music books are lost and gone; searching records, there is nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the music books are lost; searching the records, there is nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 宜選諸生，分令尋討經史百家，凡樂事無小大，皆別纂錄。

translations.literal: You should select various students and assign them to search the classics, histories, and hundred schools—every matter of music, great or small, should be separately compiled and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Select students and assign them to search the classics, histories, and hundred schools—every matter of music, great or small, should be compiled and recorded separately.

sentences.zh: 乃委一舊學，撰為樂書，以起千載絕文，以定大樑之樂。

translations.literal: Then commission one veteran scholar to compose a music book, to raise up a thousand-year broken text and fix the music of the great beam.
translations.idiomatic: Then commission one veteran scholar to compose a music book, reviving a thousand-year lost text and establishing the music of the great beam.

translations.literal: Let Five Splendors feel shame, let Six Stalks rise in embarrassment."
translations.idiomatic: Let Five Splendors feel shame and Six Stalks blush with embarrassment."

sentences.zh: 是時對樂者七十八家，鹹多引流略，浩蕩其詞，皆言樂之宜改，不言改樂之法。

translations.literal: At that time seventy-eight houses responded on music; most drew on citations and expanded their words broadly—all said music should be changed, but none said how to change music.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-eight scholars responded on music; most cited sources at length—all said music should be reformed, but none said how to reform it.

sentences.zh: 帝既素善鐘律，詳悉舊事，遂自制定禮樂。

translations.literal: The Emperor, being himself skilled in bells and pitch, knew old affairs in detail, and thereupon fixed ritual and music himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, himself skilled in bells and pitch and knowing old affairs in detail, thereupon fixed ritual and music on his own authority.

translations.literal: He also established four instruments and named them "Tong."
translations.idiomatic: He also created four instruments and named them Tong.

sentences.zh: 通受聲廣九寸，宣聲長九尺，臨岳高一寸二分。

translations.literal: The Tong's sounding chamber was nine inches wide; its sounding board nine feet long; the bridge one inch and two fen high.
translations.idiomatic: The Tong's sounding chamber was nine inches wide, its sounding board nine feet long, and the bridge one inch and two fen high.

translations.literal: On each Tong three strings were mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Each Tong carried three strings.

sentences.zh: 一曰玄英通：應鐘弦，用一百四十二絲，長四尺七寸四分差強；

translations.literal: First, the Dark Splendor Tong: the Yingzhong string used 142 threads, length four feet seven inches and a strong fraction;
translations.idiomatic: First, the Dark Splendor Tong: the Yingzhong string used 142 threads, length four feet seven inches and a strong fraction;

sentences.zh: 黃鐘弦，用二百七十絲，長九尺；

translations.literal: the Huangzhong string used 270 threads, length nine feet;
translations.idiomatic: the Huangzhong string used 270 threads, length nine feet;

sentences.zh: 大呂弦，用二百五十二絲，長八尺四寸三分差弱。

translations.literal: the Dalü string used 252 threads, length eight feet four inches and a weak fraction.
translations.idiomatic: the Dalü string used 252 threads, length eight feet four inches and a weak fraction.

sentences.zh: 二曰青陽通：太簇弦，用二百四十絲，長八尺；

translations.literal: Second, the Green Yang Tong: the Taicu string used 240 threads, length eight feet;
translations.idiomatic: Second, the Green Yang Tong: the Taicu string used 240 threads, length eight feet;

sentences.zh: 夾鐘弦，用二百二十四絲，長七尺五寸弱；

translations.literal: the Jiazhong string used 224 threads, length seven feet five inches weak;
translations.idiomatic: the Jiazhong string used 224 threads, length seven feet five inches weak;

sentences.zh: 姑洗弦，用二百一十四絲，長七尺一寸一分強。

translations.literal: the Guxian string used 214 threads, length seven feet one inch and one fen strong.
translations.idiomatic: the Guxian string used 214 threads, length seven feet one inch and one fen strong.

sentences.zh: 三曰硃明通：中呂弦，用一百九十九絲，長六尺六寸六分弱；

translations.literal: Third, the Vermilion Brightness Tong: the Zhonglü string used 199 threads, length six feet six inches and six fen weak;
translations.idiomatic: Third, the Vermilion Brightness Tong: the Zhonglü string used 199 threads, length six feet six inches and six fen weak;

sentences.zh: 蕤賓弦，用一百八十九絲，長六尺三寸二分強；

translations.literal: the Ruibin string used 189 threads, length six feet three inches and two fen strong;
translations.idiomatic: the Ruibin string used 189 threads, length six feet three inches and two fen strong;

sentences.zh: 林鐘弦，用一百八十絲，長六尺。

translations.literal: the Linzhong string used 180 threads, length six feet.
translations.idiomatic: the Linzhong string used 180 threads, length six feet.

sentences.zh: 四曰白藏通：夷則弦，用一百六十八絲，長五尺六寸二分弱；

translations.literal: Fourth, the White Storehouse Tong: the Yize string used 168 threads, length five feet six inches and two fen weak;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the White Storehouse Tong: the Yize string used 168 threads, length five feet six inches and two fen weak;

sentences.zh: 南呂弦，用一百六十絲，長五尺三寸二分大強；

translations.literal: the Nanlü string used 160 threads, length five feet three inches and two fen very strong;
translations.idiomatic: the Nanlü string used 160 threads, length five feet three inches and two fen very strong;

sentences.zh: 無射弦，用一百四十九絲，長四尺九寸九分強。

translations.literal: the Wushe string used 149 threads, length four feet nine inches and nine fen strong.
translations.idiomatic: the Wushe string used 149 threads, length four feet nine inches and nine fen strong.

sentences.zh: 因以通聲，轉推月氣，悉無差違，而還相得中。

translations.literal: Thereupon using the Tong to sound, turning to push the monthly qi, all without error or deviation, and in return attaining the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Using the Tong to produce sound and calculating the monthly qi, all matched without deviation and achieved perfect harmony.

sentences.zh: 又制為十二笛：黃鐘笛，長三尺八寸，大呂笛，長三尺六寸，太簇笛，長三尺四寸，夾鐘笛，長三尺二寸，姑洗笛，長三尺一寸，中呂笛，長二尺九寸，蕤賓笛，長二尺八寸，林鐘笛，長二尺七寸，夷則笛，長二尺六寸，南呂笛，長二尺五寸，無射笛，長二尺四寸，應鐘笛，長二尺三寸。

translations.literal: They also made twelve flutes: Huangzhong flute, length three feet eight inches; Dalü flute, three feet six inches; Taicu flute, three feet four inches; Jiazhong flute, three feet two inches; Guxian flute, three feet one inch; Zhonglü flute, two feet nine inches; Ruibin flute, two feet eight inches; Linzhong flute, two feet seven inches; Yize flute, two feet six inches; Nanlü flute, two feet five inches; Wushe flute, two feet four inches; Yingzhong flute, two feet three inches.
translations.idiomatic: They also made twelve flutes: Huangzhong at three feet eight inches, Dalü at three feet six inches, Taicu at three feet four inches, Jiazhong at three feet two inches, Guxian at three feet one inch, Zhonglü at two feet nine inches, Ruibin at two feet eight inches, Linzhong at two feet seven inches, Yize at two feet six inches, Nanlü at two feet five inches, Wushe at two feet four inches, and Yingzhong at two feet three inches.

sentences.zh: 用笛以寫通聲，飲古鐘玉律並周代古鐘，並皆不差。

translations.literal: Using the flute to write out the Tong's sound, comparing ancient bell pitch pipes with Zhou-dynasty ancient bells—all without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: Flutes were used to verify the Tong's pitch against ancient bell standards and Zhou bells—all matched perfectly.

sentences.zh: 於是被以八音，施以七聲，莫不和韻。

translations.literal: Thereupon arrayed with the eight sounds and applied with the seven tones, none failed to harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Arrayed with the eight sounds and the seven tones, everything harmonized.

sentences.zh: 是時北中郎司馬何佟之上言：「案《周禮》'王出入則奏《王夏》，屍出入則奏《肆夏》，牲出入則奏《昭夏》。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Gentleman of the Northern Army Sima He Tong memorialized: "According to the Rites of Zhou, when the king enters or exits, Xian Xia is played; when the impersonator of the dead enters or exits, Si Xia is played; when the sacrificial victim enters or exits, Zhao Xia is played.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Palace Gentleman He Tong memorialized: "The Rites of Zhou prescribe Xian Xia when the king enters or exits, Si Xia for the impersonator of the dead, and Zhao Xia for the sacrificial victim.

sentences.zh: 今樂府之《夏》，唯變《王夏》為《皇夏》，蓋緣秦、漢以來稱皇故也。

translations.literal: Now in the Music Office's Xia music, only Wang Xia was changed to Huang Xia—probably because since Qin and Han they styled themselves huang (august).
translations.idiomatic: Today's Music Office Xia pieces changed only Wang Xia to Huang Xia—likely because Qin and Han rulers styled themselves "august" (huang).

sentences.zh: 而齊氏仍宋儀注，迎神奏《昭夏》，皇帝出入奏《永至》，牲出入更奏引牲之樂。

translations.literal: Yet Qi followed Song's ritual regulations: welcoming the spirits they played Zhao Xia; when the emperor entered or exited they played Yong Zhi; when the victim entered or exited they changed to music leading the victim.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qi followed Song's ritual code: Zhao Xia welcomed the spirits, Yong Zhi accompanied the emperor's entry and exit, and separate music led the sacrificial victim.

translations.literal: The error in this could not be greater.
translations.idiomatic: The error could hardly be greater.

translations.literal: I request that the Ritual Bureau be ordered to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: I request that the Ritual Bureau correct this.

sentences.zh: 」周舍議，以為「《禮》'王入奏《王夏》'，大祭祀與朝會，其用樂一也。

translations.literal: " Zhou She argued that "The Rites says 'when the king enters, Wang Xia is played'—great sacrifices and court assemblies use the same music.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou She argued: "The Rites says 'when the king enters, Wang Xia is played'—great sacrifices and court assemblies use the same music.

sentences.zh: 而漢制，皇帝在廟，奏《永至》樂，朝會之日，別有《皇夏》。

translations.literal: Yet under Han regulations, when the emperor was in the temple Yong Zhi music was played; on days of court assembly there was a separate Huang Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han regulations, Yong Zhi was played when the emperor was in the temple, but a separate Huang Xia on court assembly days.

sentences.zh: 二樂有異，於禮為乖，宜除《永至》，還用《皇夏》。

translations.literal: The two musics differ—in ritual this is wrong; Yong Zhi should be removed and Huang Xia restored.
translations.idiomatic: Two different pieces for one rite violates ritual propriety; Yong Zhi should be abolished and Huang Xia restored.

sentences.zh: 又《禮》'屍出入奏《肆夏》，賓入大門奏《肆夏》'，則所設唯在人神，其與迎牲之樂，不可濫也。

translations.literal: Also the Rites says "when the impersonator enters or exits, Si Xia is played; when the guest enters the great gate, Si Xia is played"—thus it is set only for human and spirit; it cannot be confused with music welcoming the victim.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites also says Si Xia is played when the impersonator or guest enters the great gate—it belongs to human and spirit, and cannot be confused with music for welcoming the victim.

sentences.zh: 宋季失禮，頓虧舊則，神入廟門，遂奏《昭夏》，乃以牲牢之樂，用接祖考之靈。

translations.literal: Song at its end lost ritual and suddenly damaged old rules; when the spirit entered the temple gate they thereupon played Zhao Xia—thus using music for sacrificial victims to receive the spirits of ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Late Song lost ritual propriety: when the spirit entered the temple gate they played Zhao Xia—using victim music to receive the ancestors' spirits.

sentences.zh: 斯皆前代之深疵，當今所宜改也。

translations.literal: These are all deep flaws of former ages—matters that should be changed in the present.
translations.idiomatic: These are deep flaws of earlier dynasties that the present age should correct.

sentences.zh: 」時議又以為《周禮》雲：「若樂六變，天神皆降。

translations.literal: " At the time discussion also held that the Rites of Zhou says: "If music undergoes six transformations, the spirits of Heaven all descend.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion also cited the Rites of Zhou: "When music undergoes six transformations, the spirits of Heaven descend.

sentences.zh: 」神居上玄，去還怳忽，降則自至，迎則無所。

translations.literal: " Spirits dwell in upper mystery; going and returning are dim and fleeting—when they descend they come of themselves; to welcome them there is nowhere to go.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits dwell in upper mystery, coming and going in dim obscurity—they descend of their own accord, and there is nowhere to go to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 可改迎為降，而送依前式。

translations.literal: One may change "welcome" to "descend," while sending off follows the former form.
translations.idiomatic: Welcome should be changed to descend, while the sending-off rite follows the former form.

sentences.zh: 又《周禮》雲「若樂八變，則地祇皆出，可得而禮」，地宜依舊為迎神。

translations.literal: Also the Rites of Zhou says "if music undergoes eight transformations, then the earth spirits all emerge and can be received in ritual"—for earth, welcoming the spirit should follow the old way.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou also says that with eight musical transformations earth spirits emerge and can be received in ritual—for earth spirits, welcoming should follow the old way.

translations.literal: All were followed.
translations.idiomatic: All proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 又以明堂設樂，大略與南郊不殊，惟壇堂異名，而無就燎之位。

translations.literal: Also for music set at the Bright Hall, broadly it did not differ from the southern suburban altar, only the altar hall had a different name and there was no position for approaching the burning.
translations.idiomatic: Music at the Bright Hall broadly matched the southern suburban rite, differing only in the altar's name and lacking a position for approaching the burning.

sentences.zh: 明堂則遍歌五帝，其餘同於郊式焉。

translations.literal: At the Bright Hall they sang to all Five Emperors; the rest followed the suburban form.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall hymns addressed all Five Emperors; the rest followed the suburban form.

sentences.zh: 初宋、齊代，祀天地，祭宗廟，准漢祠太一後土，盡用宮懸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song and Qi times, sacrificing to Heaven and Earth and offering to the ancestral temple followed Han in sacrificing to Grand Unity and Earth, all using the full court bell-set.
translations.idiomatic: Early Song and Qi, sacrificing to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temple, followed Han's sacrifice to Grand Unity and Earth with full court bell-sets.

sentences.zh: 又太常任昉亦據王肅議雲：「《周官》'以六律、五聲、八音、六舞大合樂，以致鬼神，以和邦國，以諧兆庶，以安賓客，以悅遠人。

translations.literal: Also Grand Master of Ceremonies Ren Fang, citing Wang Su's argument, said: "The Offices of Zhou says 'with the six pitch pipes, five tones, eight sounds, and six dances, great music is combined to reach spirits and ghosts, harmonize the states, harmonize the myriad peoples, settle guests, and delight distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master Ren Fang, citing Wang Su, said: "The Offices of Zhou combines the six pitch pipes, five tones, eight sounds, and six dances in great music to reach spirits, harmonize the states, settle guests, and delight distant peoples.

translations.literal: " This is called the six unities—all performed at one time.
translations.idiomatic: This is called the six unities—all performed together.

sentences.zh: 今六代舞獨分用之，不厭人心。

translations.literal: Now the six dynastic dances are separately used—this does not satisfy the human heart.
translations.idiomatic: Using the six dynastic dances separately does not satisfy proper sentiment.

sentences.zh: 」遂依肅議，祀祭郊廟，備六代樂。

translations.literal: " Thereupon following Su's argument, at sacrifices, suburbs, and temples the six dynastic dances were fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: Following Su's argument, suburban and temple sacrifices included all six dynastic dances.

sentences.zh: 至是帝曰：「《周官》分樂饗祀，《虞書》止鳴兩懸，求之于古，無宮懸之議。

translations.literal: Down to this the Emperor said: "The Offices of Zhou divides music for feasting sacrifice; the Book of Yu only sounds two suspended sets—searching antiquity, there is no argument for court bell-sets.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The Offices of Zhou divides music for feasting sacrifice; the Book of Yu mentions only two suspended sets—antiquity offers no argument for full court bell-sets.

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

translations.literal: Rites for serving men are elaborate; rites for serving spirits are simple.
translations.idiomatic: Rites for serving men are elaborate; rites for serving spirits are simple.

sentences.zh: 天子襲袞，而至敬不文，觀天下之物，無可以稱其德者，則以少為貴矣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven wears the highest robe, yet utmost reverence is without ornament; viewing all things under Heaven, nothing can match his virtue—therefore the few is honored.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven wears the highest robe, yet utmost reverence avoids ornament; nothing under Heaven matches his virtue—therefore less is more honorable.

sentences.zh: 大合樂者，是使六律與五聲克諧，八音與萬舞合節耳。

translations.literal: Great combined music means making the six pitch pipes harmonize with the five tones, and the eight sounds harmonize in measure with the myriad dances—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Great combined music means harmonizing the six pitch pipes with five tones and the eight sounds with the myriad dances—that is all.

sentences.zh: 豈謂致鬼神只用六代樂也？

translations.literal: How could it mean that reaching spirits and ghosts uses only the six dynastic dances?
translations.idiomatic: How could reaching spirits require only the six dynastic dances?

sentences.zh: 其後即言'分樂序之，以祭以享。

translations.literal: Immediately after it says 'music is divided and ordered, for sacrifice and for feasting.
translations.idiomatic: Immediately after it says 'music is divided and ordered for sacrifice and feasting.

sentences.zh: '此乃曉然可明，肅則失其旨矣。

translations.literal: " This is clearly evident—Su lost the point.
translations.idiomatic: This is clearly evident—Wang Su missed the point.

sentences.zh: 推檢載籍，初無郊禋宗廟遍舞六代之文。

translations.literal: Searching records and canons, at first there is no text of the six dynastic dances performed throughout suburban, Yin, and ancestral temple rites.
translations.idiomatic: Searching records, there is no text requiring all six dynastic dances at suburban, Yin, and ancestral temple rites.

sentences.zh: 唯《明堂位》曰：'禘祀周公於太廟，硃幹玉戚，冕而舞《大武》，皮弁素積，裼而舞《大夏》。

translations.literal: Only the Record of the Bright Hall says: 'At the great temple the Duke of Zhou was honored; with vermilion shafts and jade battle-axes, wearing the cap and dancing Great Wu; with leather cap and white lower garment, baring the arm and dancing Great Xia.

translations.idiomatic: Imperial ancestor Emperor Jing's spirit chamber plays Jingde Kai Rong Dance text:

translations.literal: Imperial ancestor holding virtue; long hair its auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial ancestor holding virtue; long hair its auspice.

translations.literal: Displaying humaneness, storing application; cherishing the Way, hiding light.
translations.idiomatic: Displaying humaneness, storing application; cherishing the Way, hiding light.

translations.literal: Peaceful this sealed dwelling; joining this fragrant offering.
translations.idiomatic: Peaceful this sealed dwelling; joining this fragrant offering.

translations.literal: Forever declaring bequeathal; returning token, cutting Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Forever declaring bequeathal; returning token, cutting Shang.

sentences.zh: 皇考高祖武皇帝神室奏《武德舞》辭：

translations.literal: Imperial father Emperor Wu's spirit chamber plays Wude Dance text:
translations.idiomatic: Imperial father Emperor Wu's spirit chamber plays Wude Dance text:

translations.literal: Abundant the sage ancestor; comforting fortune, rising in Li.
translations.idiomatic: Abundant the sage ancestor; comforting fortune, rising in Li.

translations.literal: Way circling warp and woof; merit reaching dark spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Way circling warp and woof; merit reaching dark spirits.

translations.literal: Square chariot surpassing Hu; compared to Shun, surpassing Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Square chariot surpassing Hu; compared to Shun, surpassing Gui.

translations.literal: Bright brightness is chanted; reverent brightness is here.
translations.idiomatic: Bright brightness is chanted; reverent brightness is here.

translations.literal: Cloud and thunder meeting difficulty; charting south, together rising.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud and thunder meeting difficulty; charting south, together rising.

translations.literal: Great settling Yang and Yue; shaking prestige Heng and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Great settling Yang and Yue; shaking prestige Heng and Chu.

translations.literal: Four inner domains dwelling in heart; nine categories returning to order.
translations.idiomatic: Four inner domains dwelling in heart; nine categories returning to order.

translations.literal: Auspicious star issuing from wings; not clouds entering Lü.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious star issuing from wings; not clouds entering Lü.

translations.literal: Virtue flowing, bearing in speech; celebration bright, feather adornment.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue flowing, bearing in speech; celebration bright, feather adornment.

translations.literal: How reverent the clear temple; displaying raised emblem and merit.
translations.idiomatic: How reverent the clear temple; displaying raised emblem and merit.

translations.literal: Fine jade already displayed; abundant offerings thus pure.
translations.idiomatic: Fine jade already displayed; abundant offerings thus pure.

translations.literal: This will feast, this will enjoy—grand plan without end.
translations.idiomatic: This will feast, this will enjoy—grand plan without end.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，文帝始定圓丘、明堂及宗廟樂。

translations.literal: In Tianjia year 1, Emperor Wen first fixed Round Altar, Bright Hall, and ancestral temple music.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 1, Emperor Wen first fixed Round Altar, Bright Hall, and ancestral temple music.

sentences.zh: 都官尚書到仲舉權奏：「眾官入出，皆奏《肅成》。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Dao Zhongju provisionally memorialized: "When officials enter and exit, all play Su Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Dao Zhongju provisionally memorialized: "When officials enter and exit, all play Su Cheng.

translations.literal: When victims enter and exit, play Yin Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When victims enter and exit, play Yin Xi.

translations.literal: Presenting hair and blood, play Jia Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting hair and blood, play Jia Jian.

translations.literal: Welcoming and sending spirits, play Zhao Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming and sending spirits, play Zhao Xia.

translations.literal: When the emperor enters the altar, play Yong Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor enters the altar, play Yong Zhi.

translations.literal: When the emperor ascends the steps, play ascent song.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascends the steps, play ascent song.

sentences.zh: 皇帝初獻及太尉亞獻、光祿勳終獻，並奏《宣烈》。

translations.literal: Emperor's first presentation and Grand Commandant's second presentation, Director of Ceremonies' final presentation—all play Xuan Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor's first presentation and Grand Commandant's second presentation, Director of Ceremonies' final presentation—all play Xuan Lie.

translations.literal: When the emperor drinks blessing wine, play Jia Zuo;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor drinks blessing wine, play Jia Zuo;

translations.literal: At the burning position, play Zhao Yuan;
translations.idiomatic: At the burning position, play Zhao Yuan;

translations.literal: Returning to the side hall, play Xiu Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the side hall, play Xiu Cheng.

sentences.zh: 至太建元年，定三朝之樂，采梁故事：第一，奏《相和》五引，各隨王月，則先奏其鐘。

translations.literal: Down to Taijian year 1, fixing three court audience music—adopting Liang precedents: first, play Harmonizing Five Introductions, each following the monthly master—then first play its bell.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Taijian year 1, fixing three court audience music—adopting Liang precedents: first, play Harmonizing Five Introductions, each following the monthly master—then first play its bell.

sentences.zh: 唯眾官入，奏《俊雅》，林鐘作，太簇參應之，取其臣道也。

translations.literal: Only when officials enter, play Jun Ya—Linzhong playing, Taicu participating in response, taking the minister's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Only when officials enter, play Jun Ya—Linzhong playing, Taicu participating in response, taking the minister's Way.

translations.literal: Impromptu music plays.
translations.idiomatic: Impromptu music plays.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出閣，奏《皇雅》，黃鐘作，太簇、夾鐘、姑洗、大呂皆應之。

translations.literal: When the emperor exits the side chamber, play Huang Ya—Huangzhong playing, Taicu, Jiazhong, Guxian, Dalü all responding.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor exits the side chamber, play Huang Ya—Huangzhong playing, Taicu, Jiazhong, Guxian, Dalü all responding.

translations.literal: Impromptu music plays.
translations.idiomatic: Impromptu music plays.

sentences.zh: 皇太子入至十字陛，奏《胤雅》，太簇作，南呂參應之，取其二月少陽也。

translations.literal: When the crown prince enters to the cross-shaped steps, play Yin Ya—Taicu playing, Nanlü participating in response, taking its second month's lesser yang.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince enters to the cross-shaped steps, play Yin Ya—Taicu playing, Nanlü participating in response, taking its second month's lesser yang.

sentences.zh: 皇帝延王公登，奏《寅雅》，夷則作，夾鐘應之，取其月法也。

translations.literal: When the emperor extends to kings and dukes ascending, play Yin Ya—Yize playing, Jiazhong responding, taking its monthly method.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor extends to kings and dukes ascending, play Yin Ya—Yize playing, Jiazhong responding, taking its monthly method.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入甯變服，奏《皇雅》，黃鐘作，林鐘參應之。

translations.literal: When the emperor enters the resting chamber to change robes, play Huang Ya—Huangzhong playing, Linzhong participating in response.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor enters the resting chamber to change robes, play Huang Ya—Huangzhong playing, Linzhong participating in response.

translations.literal: Impromptu music plays.
translations.idiomatic: Impromptu music plays.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出甯及升座，皆奏《皇雅》，並如變服之作。

translations.literal: When the emperor exits the chamber and ascends the seat, all play Huang Ya—same as the robe-changing performance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor exits the chamber and ascends the seat, all play Huang Ya—same as the robe-changing performance.

sentences.zh: 上壽酒，奏《介雅》，太簇作，南呂參應之，取其陽氣盛長，萬物輻湊也。

translations.literal: At the longevity wine, play Jie Ya—Taicu playing, Nanlü participating in response, taking its yang qi flourishing long, myriad things converging.
translations.idiomatic: At the longevity wine, play Jie Ya—Taicu playing, Nanlü participating in response, taking its yang qi flourishing long, myriad things converging.

sentences.zh: 食舉，奏《需雅》，蕤賓作，大呂參應之，取火主於禮，所謂「食我以禮」也。

translations.literal: At food presentation, play Xu Ya—Ruibin playing, Dalü participating in response, taking fire mastering ritual—what is called "feeding me with ritual."
translations.idiomatic: At food presentation, play Xu Ya—Ruibin playing, Dalü participating in response, taking fire mastering ritual—what is called "feeding me with ritual."

sentences.zh: 撤饌，奏《雍雅》，無射作，中呂參應之，取其津潤已竭也。

translations.literal: At clearing dishes, play Yong Ya—Wushe playing, Zhonglü participating in response, taking its moisture already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At clearing dishes, play Yong Ya—Wushe playing, Zhonglü participating in response, taking its moisture already exhausted.

sentences.zh: 武舞奏《大壯》，夷則作，夾鐘參應之，七月金始王，取其堅斷也。

translations.literal: Martial dance plays Great Zhuang—Yize playing, Jiazhong participating in response; seventh month metal begins mastery, taking its firm cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Martial dance plays Great Zhuang—Yize playing, Jiazhong participating in response; seventh month metal begins mastery, taking its firm cutting.

translations.literal: Impromptu music leading back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Impromptu music leading back and forth.

sentences.zh: 文舞奏《大觀》，姑洗作，應鐘參應之，三月萬物必榮，取其布惠者也。

translations.literal: Civil dance plays Great Guan—Guxian playing, Yingzhong participating in response; third month myriad things must flourish, taking its spreading bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Civil dance plays Great Guan—Guxian playing, Yingzhong participating in response; third month myriad things must flourish, taking its spreading bounty.

translations.literal: Impromptu music leading back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Impromptu music leading back and forth.

sentences.zh: 眾官出，奏《俊雅》，蕤賓作，林鐘、夷則、南呂、無射、應鐘、太簇參應之。

translations.literal: When officials exit, play Jun Ya—Ruibin playing, Linzhong, Yize, Nanlü, Wushe, Yingzhong, Taicu all participating in response.
translations.idiomatic: When officials exit, play Jun Ya—Ruibin playing, Linzhong, Yize, Nanlü, Wushe, Yingzhong, Taicu all participating in response.

translations.literal: Impromptu music plays.
translations.idiomatic: Impromptu music plays.

sentences.zh: 皇帝起，奏《皇雅》，黃鐘作，林鐘、夷則、南呂、無射參應之。

translations.literal: When the emperor rises, play Huang Ya—Huangzhong playing, Linzhong, Yize, Nanlü, Wushe all participating in response.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor rises, play Huang Ya—Huangzhong playing, Linzhong, Yize, Nanlü, Wushe all participating in response.

translations.literal: Impromptu music plays.
translations.idiomatic: Impromptu music plays.

sentences.zh: 祠用宋曲，宴准梁樂，蓋取人神不雜也。

translations.literal: For sacrifice use Song tunes; for feasts follow Liang music—generally taking human and spirit not mixed.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifice use Song tunes; for feasts follow Liang music—generally taking human and spirit not mixed.

translations.literal: Imperial decree: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial decree: "Approved."

sentences.zh: 五年，詔尚書左丞劉平、儀曹郎張崖定南北郊及明堂儀注。

translations.literal: In year 5, ordered Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Ping and Gentleman of Ritual Affairs Zhang Ya to fix southern and northern suburb and Bright Hall ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, ordered Left Assistant Director Liu Ping and Gentleman of Ritual Affairs Zhang Ya to fix southern and northern suburb and Bright Hall ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 改天嘉中所用齊樂，盡以韶為名。

translations.literal: Changed the Qi music used in Tianjia to all take Shao as name.
translations.idiomatic: Changed the Qi music used in Tianjia to all take Shao as name.

sentences.zh: 工就位定，協律校尉舉麾，太樂令跪贊雲：「奏《懋韶》之樂。

translations.literal: Performers in position fixed; pitch-harmonizing adjutant raises the baton; Grand Music Director kneels praising: "Play Mao Shao music."
translations.idiomatic: Performers in position fixed; pitch-harmonizing adjutant raises the baton; Grand Music Director kneels praising: "Play Mao Shao music."

translations.literal: Sending down spirits, play Tong Shao;
translations.idiomatic: Sending down spirits, play Tong Shao;

translations.literal: When victims enter and exit, play Jie Shao;
translations.idiomatic: When victims enter and exit, play Jie Shao;

sentences.zh: 帝入壇及還便殿，奏《穆韶》。

translations.literal: When the emperor enters the altar and returns to the side hall, play Mu Shao.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor enters the altar and returns to the side hall, play Mu Shao.

sentences.zh: 帝初再拜，舞《七德》，工執幹楯，曲終複綴。

translations.literal: Emperor's first two bows—dance Seven Virtues; performers holding shields and spears; at song's end, repeat and join.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor's first two bows—dance Seven Virtues; performers holding shields and spears; at song's end, repeat and join.

sentences.zh: 出就懸東，繼舞《九序》，工執羽籥。

translations.literal: Exit toward the east of the suspension, then dance Nine Sequence; performers holding feathers and flutes.
translations.idiomatic: Exit toward the east of the suspension, then dance Nine Sequence; performers holding feathers and flutes.

sentences.zh: 獻爵于天神及太祖之座，奏登歌。

translations.literal: Presenting goblets to the Heaven spirit and Grand Ancestor's seat, play ascent song.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting goblets to the Heaven spirit and Grand Ancestor's seat, play ascent song.

translations.literal: When the emperor drinks blessing wine, play Jia Shao;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor drinks blessing wine, play Jia Shao;

translations.literal: Approaching the burning outlook, play Bao Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Approaching the burning outlook, play Bao Shao.

sentences.zh: 至六年十一月，侍中尚書左僕射、建昌侯徐陵，儀曹郎中沈罕奏來年元會儀注，稱舍人蔡景曆奉敕，先會一日，太樂展宮懸、高糸亙、五案於殿庭。

translations.literal: Down to the eleventh month of year 6, Attendant Cavalier, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, Marquis of Jianchang Xu Ling, and Gentleman of Ritual Affairs Shen Han memorialized next year's New Year assembly ritual regulations, saying Palace Attendant Cai Jingli received the edict: one day before the assembly, Grand Music displays court bell-set, high rope, five stands in the hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the eleventh month of year 6, Attendant Cavalier Xu Ling and Gentleman of Ritual Affairs Shen Han memorialized next year's New Year assembly ritual regulations, saying Palace Attendant Cai Jingli received the edict: one day before the assembly, Grand Music displays court bell-set, high rope, five stands in the hall courtyard.

translations.literal: When guests enter, play Harmonizing Five Introductions.
translations.idiomatic: When guests enter, play Harmonizing Five Introductions.

sentences.zh: 帝出，黃門侍郎舉麾于殿上，掌故應之，舉於階下，奏《康韶》之樂。

translations.literal: When the emperor exits, the Palace Gentleman raises the baton in the hall; the music master responds, raising at the steps below—play Kang Shao music.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor exits, the Palace Gentleman raises the baton in the hall; the music master responds, raising at the steps below—play Kang Shao music.

translations.literal: Edict extending to kings and dukes ascending, play Bian Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Edict extending to kings and dukes ascending, play Bian Shao.

sentences.zh: 奉珪璧訖，初引下殿，奏亦如之。

translations.literal: Presenting jade disks finished, first leading below the hall—playing also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting jade disks finished, first leading below the hall—playing also the same.

translations.literal: When the emperor rises, entering the side hall, play Mu Shao.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor rises, entering the side hall, play Mu Shao.

translations.literal: Changing robes and exiting again—playing also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Changing robes and exiting again—playing also the same.

translations.literal: When the emperor raises wine, play Sui Shao.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor raises wine, play Sui Shao.

translations.literal: Presenting dishes, play You Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting dishes, play You Shao.

sentences.zh: 帝禦茶果，太常丞跪請進舞《七德》，繼之《九序》。

translations.literal: When the emperor receives tea and fruit, Grand Master of Ceremonies Assistant kneels requesting advancing dance Seven Virtues, followed by Nine Sequence.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor receives tea and fruit, Grand Master of Ceremonies Assistant kneels requesting advancing dance Seven Virtues, followed by Nine Sequence.

sentences.zh: 其鼓吹雜伎，取晉、宋之舊，微更附益。

translations.literal: Its impromptu acrobatics took Jin and Song old forms, slightly changed and supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Its impromptu acrobatics took Jin and Song old forms, slightly changed and supplemented.

sentences.zh: 舊元會有黃龍變、文鹿、師子之類，太建初定制，皆除之。

translations.literal: Formerly the New Year assembly had yellow dragon transformation, patterned deer, lion and similar types—in Taijian early fixed regulations, all were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the New Year assembly had yellow dragon transformation, patterned deer, lion and similar types—in Taijian early fixed regulations, all were removed.

sentences.zh: 至是蔡景曆奏，悉複設焉。

translations.literal: At this time Cai Jingli memorialized—all were restored.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Cai Jingli memorialized—all were restored.

sentences.zh: 其制，鼓吹一部十六人，則簫十三人，笳二人，鼓一人。

translations.literal: Its regulation: one impromptu music section sixteen persons—then thirteen xiao players, two jia players, one drum player.
translations.idiomatic: Its regulation: one impromptu music section sixteen persons—thirteen xiao players, two jia players, one drum player.

sentences.zh: 東宮一部，降三人，簫減二人，笳減一人。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace one section, reduced three persons—xiao reduced two, jia reduced one.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Palace one section, reduced three persons—xiao reduced two, jia reduced one.

sentences.zh: 諸王一部，又降一人，減簫一。

translations.literal: Kings one section, again reduced one person, xiao reduced one.
translations.idiomatic: Kings one section, again reduced one person, xiao reduced one.

sentences.zh: 庶姓一部，又降一人，複減簫一。

translations.literal: Common surname one section, again reduced one person, again xiao reduced one.
translations.idiomatic: Common surname one section, again reduced one person, again xiao reduced one.

sentences.zh: 及後主嗣位，耽荒於酒，視朝之外，多在宴筵。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord succeeded, indulging in wine, outside court audiences mostly at banquets.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord succeeded, indulging in wine, outside court audiences mostly at banquets.

sentences.zh: 尤重聲樂，遣宮女習北方簫鼓，謂之《代北》，酒酣則奏之。

translations.literal: Especially valuing sound and music, sending palace women to learn northern xiao and drums, called Dai Bei—when deep in wine then playing it.
translations.idiomatic: Especially valuing sound and music, sending palace women to learn northern xiao and drums, called Dai Bei—when deep in wine then playing it.

sentences.zh: 又于清樂中造《黃鸝留》及《玉樹後庭花》、《金釵兩臂垂》等曲，與幸臣等制其歌詞，綺豔相高，極於輕薄。

translations.literal: Also among clear music made Yellow Oriole Staying, Jade Tree Courtyard Flower, Golden Hairpin Two Arms Hanging and other tunes—with favorite ministers composing their song texts, ornate and lofty mutually surpassing, extreme in lightness and frivolity.
translations.idiomatic: Also among clear music made Yellow Oriole Staying, Jade Tree Courtyard Flower, Golden Hairpin Two Arms Hanging and other tunes—with favorite ministers composing their song texts, ornate and lofty mutually surpassing, extreme in lightness and frivolity.

translations.literal: Men and women singing in alternation—its sound very mournful.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women singing in alternation—its sound very mournful.
